title: How to organise the lawn and garden tool zone | Garage
description:
Stores the yard tools and outdoor supplies so long handles stay off the floor and garden chemicals stay latched away from everything else.

This is the Lawn and Garden Tool Zone in the Garage. About 60-90 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Every long-handled tool hanging head-up on the rail with nothing leaning in a corner, the hose coiled on its reel beside the door it goes out of, and all garden chemicals in their original labelled containers behind a latch above head height.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Out go the rake with three tines left, the hose with the split you have meant to patch for two summers, and th
Straighten: Long handles hang head-up on a rail so no fork stands loose in a corner waiting to be trodden on.
Shine: Scrape caked soil off the spade and hoe blades, wipe them with an oily rag, and run a file along the spade edg
Safety: Garden chemicals stay in their original labelled containers on a latched shelf above child and pet height, nev
Standardize: A painted or taped strip on the wall behind each long handle, so a bare strip is a question you answer before
Sustain: The mower needs to cool before it goes away anyway, and that is the window when the spade gets scraped, wiped,

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every long tool hangs on its taped strip, and nothing but garden chemicals lives on the latched shelf.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/garage-the-lawn-and-garden-tool-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
